fixes.explanation: That's it, baker. The LORD says, "The LORD rebukes you, Satan!" (Zechariah 3:2). Satan is there to accuse, and the LORD is the one who speaks up. Then He asks, "Is not this man a firebrand snatched from the fire?" (Zechariah 3:2).
Good guess, baker, because Satan is there to accuse. But the LORD doesn't say anything like that. He says, "The LORD rebukes you, Satan!" (Zechariah 3:2). The rebuke is His whole answer to Satan.

That's right, baker. The angel of the LORD gives Joshua a charge from the LORD of Hosts: "If you walk in My ways and keep My instructions…" (Zechariah 3:7). Notice that this comes right after Joshua's clothes are changed. That's a big job, and I'm glad it came after the new robes.

Wall building is a real job, baker, but it's not this charge. The angel of the LORD gives Joshua a charge from the LORD of Hosts: "If you walk in My ways and keep My instructions…" (Zechariah 3:7). It's about how Joshua lives, not a construction project.

Joshua is a priest, so I see why you'd go there, baker. But this charge doesn't mention a lamb or an altar. The angel of the LORD gives Joshua a charge from the LORD of Hosts: "If you walk in My ways and keep My instructions…" (Zechariah 3:7).

Helping with a building project sounds like a good neighborly thing, baker, but it's not what this verse says. The LORD of Hosts says, "…you will each invite your neighbor to sit under your own vine and fig tree." (Zechariah 3:10). The invitation is to sit down, not to start working.
